einzeiler: Ashley Kahn on the making and legacy of Paul Simon's iconic album Graceland
kurzfassung: Author Ashley Kahn joins the podcast to discuss his book about Paul Simon's seminal album, Graceland. The hosts explore how Simon fused South African township music with his own style during the height of apartheid. They also examine the album's lasting cultural impact, the controversy surrounding it, and the unique recording process.
stichpunkte: Ashley Kahn discusses his book Days of Miracle and Wonder, focusing on Paul Simon's Graceland.
The album was inspired by a bootleg cassette of South African township music.
Paul Simon chose to travel to South Africa to collaborate directly with local musicians despite political tensions.
The project faced a cultural boycott and significant controversy surrounding apartheid.
Simon ensured the South African artists were properly credited and paid triple the standard American union scale.
Engineer Roy Halley utilized early digital editing tools to cut, paste, and structure the songs.
The title track explores themes of middle age, mortality, and visiting Elvis Presley's grave.
The song Homeless originated as a Zulu wedding phrase that Simon paired with melody.
Simon self-funded the subsequent concert tour to keep the original international musicians together.

clips.hook: Capturing an optimistic mid-80s cultural moment
clips.text: The book aims to chronicle an unusual period in the mid-to-late 1980s when political and cultural borders felt open and optimistic.

clips.hook: Creating a masterpiece in under three weeks
clips.text: The album evolved from a brief trip of less than three weeks where Simon met the participating musicians for the first time.

clips.hook: Tripling union scale and honoring the original artists
clips.text: Simon paid triple the standard American studio rates and insisted on touring with the exact musicians who played on the record.

clips.hook: Turning a Zulu wedding song into a track about homelessness
clips.text: Simon took a joyful traditional Zulu wedding song about lacking basic necessities and repeatedly integrated the word homeless into it.

clips.hook: Singing the new South African national anthem on stage
clips.text: During a college concert appearance, Ladysmith Black Mambazo performed various songs, including a cover from Sesame Street, and closed by singing their newly united nation's national anthem.

beschreibung:
Graceland, by the great Paul Simon, was always a big deal in our house. From the Boy in the Bubble to the Myth of Fingerprints, it was on almost constant repeat, the soundtrack of my childhood. Ashley Kahn’s book,
Days of Miracle and Wonder, is a thorough, beautifully researched compendium of how the album was made. A real examination of Simon’s genius, this book breaks down the album and its effects on the music industry and the world. Join us as we discuss a seminal moment in music history, and a terrific book.
